_note: The hours of the day. Ours: a sky palette is art direction and not a published number, so these are tuned by eye against the CC0 HDRIs they ship with (Poly Haven, fetched by tools/fetch-assets.ts). One sky meant every match was the same hour of the same day, and the light does more for how a map reads than any amount of geometry.
_hdr: The environment map, for reflections and ambient light. A MeshStandardMaterial with metalness reflects its environment, and with nothing to reflect every metal surface renders pure BLACK, so this is load-bearing and not decoration. A missing file falls back to sky.hdr, which means a checkout that has not run `npm run assets` still renders.
_colors: zenith, horizon and ground are the three bands of the authored dome (src/game/sky.ts) and sun is the disk. Hex strings, because a palette is read and edited by eye far more often than it is computed. The dome is authored rather than photographic because a photo's horizon sits at a fixed height that does not line up with where our ground plane ends.
_sun: dir is the direction the light comes FROM and is normalised by the code. intensity is the directional light's; env is scene.environmentIntensity, which at full strength fills every shadow straight back in and costs the scene its contrast.
_fog: near and far in metres. The battle royale scales both up because its map is 440 m across and the range is 80 m.
